title: Maple's asynchronous redemption forced Obex to add Instance-specific functions the general vault standards do not cover
content:
The Maple USDC Instance is the case where the Instance-specific Operational Processes slot — reserved everywhere for procedures "that deviate from or otherwise supplement the general … Liquidity Layer processes" — actually carries content. It defines two calls: `requestMapleRedemption(address mapleToken, uint256 shares)` (A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.3.1.1) and `cancelMapleRedemption(address mapleToken, uint256 shares)` (…3.1.2).

The first is a two-phase exit: the contract "will submit a redemption request to the vault. Assets will not be received immediately; they must be claimed in a separate step after the vault processes the redemption" — the same shape as the generic ERC-7540 path, but Maple-specific. The second has no generic equivalent anywhere in the general process definitions: the ability to *retract* a pending redemption, "removing the specified number of shares from the pending redemption."

Cancellation matters because an asynchronous redemption is a standing commitment to exit at whatever terms apply when the vault processes it. Without a cancel, an operator who requests an exit and then sees conditions change is locked into the consequence of a decision made under stale information.

One detail is a genuine trap. `cancelMapleRedemption` "will check that a rate limit exists for the asset. If no rate limit exists the transaction will revert." Because rate limit configuration is also the whitelist, and only Sky Governance can write it, **removing Maple's rate limit would strand any pending redemption in an uncancellable state**. Delisting a venue and unwinding positions in it are therefore order-dependent operations, and nothing in the Artifact records that dependency.
description: requestMapleRedemption and cancelMapleRedemption fill the Instance-level "deviate or supplement" slot, giving the relayer a way to withdraw a pending redemption request before it settles.
